title: Security FAQ Refresh (2026) — Working Outline + Owners + Open Questions
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the working outline for the refreshed Enterprise Security FAQ (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- It should be: (1) field-friendly, (2) aligned to current product behavior, (3) consistent with approved claims language, and (4) easy to cite in RFPs (version + last reviewed + evidence process).

Non-goals / guardrails
- Do not promise roadmap items.
- If capability differs by deployment mode, state it explicitly.
- Avoid absolute statements unless we have evidence + Security/GRC sign-off.
- Anything involving contractual terms (breach notification timelines, indemnity, SLAs) must be reviewed by Legal (Michael Grant) + Commercial (Sofia Mendes) before publishing.

Primary audience
- AEs, SEs, CS (for handoffs), customer security teams.

Publishing targets
- Canonical: Confluence (Sales Enablement > Security FAQ)
- Secondary: redwood-docs public “Enterprise Security Overview” page (high-level + gated evidence request)
- Snippets: internal admin/snippet tool (per PR-39122)

Owners & workflow (draft)
- Program mgmt / process: Talia Benson
- Technical accuracy: Marcus Lin + Kevin Osei
- GRC/compliance language: Olga Petrov + Daniel Carter
- Product alignment (no-roadmap promises): Naomi Feldman
- Deployment specifics (Dedicated/Private): Markus Klein / Fatima Noor / Colin O’Donnell
- Messaging & consistency: Camila Reyes + Soojin Lee
- Docs publish + formatting: Elliot Price (Confluence) + Kira Thompson / Wei Chen (docs site)

Timeline checkpoint targets (suggested)
- 2026-02-14: lock outline + open-questions list (this doc)
- 2026-02-21: draft content complete + claims matrix references inserted
- 2026-02-28: review cycle complete (Security/GRC/PMM/Legal)
- 2026-03-05: publish to Confluence + update docs links
- 2026-03-07: sales enablement training + HubSpot snippet update

Outline (proposed FAQ structure)

0) Front matter (required on page)
Owner: Talia Benson
Reviewers: Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov, Naomi Feldman, Camila Reyes
Content includes:
- What this FAQ covers / does not cover
- Deployment modes: Hosted, Dedicated, Private (quick definitions)
- “How to use this FAQ in RFPs” (cite version/date; do not paraphrase sensitive claims)
- Evidence request process link + NDA note
- Last reviewed date + next scheduled review

Open questions
- Do we want one FAQ with mode callouts, or separate pages per mode + shared index?
- What’s the standard citation format for RFPs? (ex: “Redwood Enterprise Security FAQ v2026.02”)

Sources
- Slack: #sales/1768729031-rfp-library-where-are-we-storing-final-language
- Confluence: rfp-response-ownership-and-approvals


1) Platform overview + shared responsibility model
Owner: Naomi Feldman (with Markus Klein for mode details)
Purpose: establish boundaries (what Redwood controls vs customer controls) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Must include:
- Components: API/SDK, control plane, data plane, customer org/project
- For Private: network ownership boundaries (customer VPC/on-prem) + what Redwood manages (control plane, updates, etc.)
- For Dedicated: isolation model (dedicated GPU pools) without over-claiming “single-tenant everything” unless true

Open questions
- Dedicated: clarify what is “dedicated” (GPU pools) vs shared control plane (if applicable). Need exact wording.
- Private: confirm update mechanism & who applies patches (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed) in on-prem scenarios.

Sources
- Fireflies: 2025-12-12 Summit Insurance deep dive (Private controls)
- Slack: #sales/1769537745-private-deployment-security-appendix-needed


2) Security program overview (policies, governance, risk)
Owner: Olga Petrov
Includes:
- Security governance and ownership
- Risk management approach (high-level)
- Security training (internal)
- Vendor/subprocessor management (pointer to subprocessor list process)

Open questions
- What can we say about third-party risk tooling (if any) without naming vendors?

Sources
- Field asks from Acme Health + Helix Pharma calls (questionnaires ask “describe program”)


3) Compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO alignment, other frameworks)
Owner: Daniel Carter (review: Olga Petrov; messaging: Camila Reyes)
Sections
3.1 SOC 2
- Current status + scope summary (no audit-period specifics here unless GRC provides the finalized line)
- How to request the report (NDA required)
- Control themes mapped to product
3.2 ISO 27001 alignment (IMPORTANT: avoid misrepresentation)
- Approved language: “aligns with”, “maps to”, “supports controls” — NOT “certified” unless actually certified
- Offer a mapping summary (Annex A themes)
3.3 Other: HIPAA/BAA, PCI, GDPR
- Keep this as “supporting controls” + “we can sign DPA / discuss BAA via Legal” style language; do not claim certification.

Open questions
- Final approved ISO language (see #sales thread). Confirm exact phrase with GRC.
- HIPAA: do we have an approved “we do/do not sign BAA” line for Hosted vs Private?

Sources
- Slack: #sales/1769411188-what-do-we-say-about-iso27001
- Fireflies: 2025-11-05 Acme Health (BAA/HIPAA questions)
- Fireflies: 2026-02-03 Helix Pharma procurement/legal/security


4) Data handling & data use (customer data, prompts, outputs)
Owner: Naomi Feldman (review: Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov)
Must answer clearly:
- What is “Customer Content” (prompts, inputs, outputs)
- Whether customer content is used to train models (Hosted/Dedicated/Private). Avoid ambiguity.
- Support/operations access to customer content (when/why, approvals)
- Data classification (what we store where)

Open questions
- Confirm exact “no training” wording aligned across FAQ, public docs, and RFP library (avoid “never” if there are narrow exceptions like opt-in evals).
- Confirm whether any default logging includes prompt text (and by mode).

Sources
- Jira: SUP-28790 (repeat question on training)
- Slack: #sales/1768451123 (FAQ refresh questions)


5) Data retention, deletion, and data residency
Owner: Olga Petrov (review: Lukas Meyer for EMEA nuance; Marcus Lin for technical behavior)
Subsections
5.1 Retention (by data type)
- Request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts)
- Prompt/response content (if stored at all) and retention if enabled
- Audit logs (retention options)
- Backups (high-level statement)
5.2 Deletion
- How customers request deletion (API/Support) + expected timelines (avoid hard SLA unless approved)
- What deletion covers (primary systems vs backups, with standard caveat)
5.3 Residency
- Regional processing options by mode
- EU residency requirements: what we can/can’t guarantee; tie to deployment mode and region selection
- Private: strongest residency control (customer network) — still define any telemetry/control plane metadata routing

Open questions
- Need definitive table: “data type x mode x default retention x configurable?”
- Confirm wording for “processing region” vs “data at rest region” (avoid mixing terms).
- Private mode telemetry: what leaves the customer network? (metrics? logs?) Need exact list.

Sources
- Slack: #sales/1769014420 (EU residency objections)
- Slack: #eng-security/1769226604 (retention wording review)
- Fireflies: 2026-01-16 Nordbank RFP kickoff (EU constraints)


6) Encryption & key management (KMS/HSM)
Owner: Marcus Lin (review: Kevin Osei; deployment specifics: Colin O’Donnell)
Sections
6.1 Encryption in transit
- TLS, API endpoints, mTLS options (only if supported)
6.2 Encryption at rest
- Storage encryption summary
6.3 Key management boundaries
- Hosted: Redwood-managed keys (with cloud KMS)
- Dedicated: clarify if customer-specific keys possible and how
- Private: customer-managed keys / KMS integration options; HSM mention only if actually supported
6.4 Customer responsibilities
- Key rotation on customer side (Private)

Open questions
- Confirm whether any mode supports customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption (CMK) today vs “on request” (danger zone).
- Confirm exact HSM phrasing (supported integrations vs “compatible with”).

Sources
- Slack: #sales/1769302209 (encryption/KMS one-pager reviewers)
- Fireflies: Aurora Financial SSO + audit logs review (also asked about encryption/KMS)


7) Identity, SSO/SAML, SCIM, and RBAC
Owner: Markus Klein (content), reviewer: Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
Need crisp answers to typical questionnaires:
- SSO: SAML 2.0 support + supported IdPs (list only if we’re comfortable maintaining it)
- SCIM: what objects are supported (users, groups) and limitations
- RBAC roles: what roles exist + granularity; console + API coverage
- MFA: if enforced via IdP vs native
- Service accounts / API keys: management + rotation expectations

Open questions
- Confirm current RBAC roles/permissions summary source of truth (PR-612).
- Confirm whether SCIM supports group-based role assignment.

Sources
- Fireflies: 2026-02-20 Aurora Financial (SSO/SCIM/audit logs)
- Confluence: sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities
- GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-612


8) Audit logging & monitoring
Owner: Kevin Osei (review: Marcus Lin; docs: Elliot Price)
Sections
- What events are logged (taxonomy)
- What fields are included (actor, timestamp, object, IP, request id, etc.)
- Export options (SIEM/S3/etc.) and limitations
- Retention options + pricing packaging caveat (don’t quote prices)

Open questions
- Confirm event list is accurate for both Console and API actions.
- Confirm export destinations currently supported vs “planned”.

Sources
- Slack: #eng-security/1769055512 (audit log export questions)
- GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-2849
- Confluence: audit-logging-customer-overview


9) Vulnerability management & secure SDLC
Owner: Marcus Lin
Include
- Vulnerability scanning (high level)
- Dependency management approach (high level)
- Pen testing language (frequency phrasing must be approved)
- Responsible disclosure / security contact

Open questions
- Approved pen test phrasing (“periodic”, “at least annually”, etc.) per Security + GRC.

Sources
- Slack: #eng-security/1769483377 (pen test frequency)
- Fireflies: Helix Pharma (vuln mgmt expectations)


10) Incident response, breach notification, and business continuity
Owner: Olga Petrov (GRC) + Marcus Lin (technical)
Include
- IR program overview
- Customer notification approach (avoid contractual timelines unless Legal-approved)
- BCP/DR summary (high-level) + redundancy by region (only if accurate)

Open questions
- What is the approved default “notification” statement for questionnaires?

Sources
- Fireflies: Helix Pharma procurement/legal/security sync


11) Subprocessors and third parties
Owner: Daniel Carter
Include
- How we manage subprocessors
- How customers can request the current list (canonical location)
- Data categories shared with subprocessors (high level)

Open questions
- Confirm whether we can share the full list publicly or only under NDA.

Sources
- Gmail thread: Lukas Meyer DPA + subprocessor list request


12) Private deployment appendix (if we keep within same FAQ)
Owner: Colin O’Donnell (review: Fatima Noor)
Goal: answer Private RFP deep dives without cluttering the main FAQ.
Include
- Network topology options (VPC / on-prem)
- Isolation boundaries + customer controls
- Update & patching responsibilities
- Logging/telemetry behavior

Open questions
- Need a crisp diagram reference (Design ticket DES-2924). Where will it live and how do we link it?

Sources
- Slack: #sales/1769537745 (private appendix)
- Linear: DES-2924 (data flow diagram)


13) Evidence requests & how to run a security review with Redwood
Owner: Daniel Carter (process) + Talia Benson (field-friendly wording)
Include
- What is available under NDA (SOC 2 report, pen test summary if available, policies, etc.)
- Where to submit requests (intake form / ticket)
- SLAs / expected turnaround ranges (approved only)
- Escalation path for urgent deals

Open questions
- Confirm “standard turnaround time” language with GRC; align to triage queue process.

Sources
- Confluence: soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook
- Gmail: Aisha Rahman urgent evidence escalation (Aurora)
- Confluence: CS escalation playbook (security review handoff)


14) FAQ glossary + definitions (to reduce bad paraphrasing)
Owner: Camila Reyes (messaging) + Naomi Feldman (accuracy)
Include
- “Hosted”, “Dedicated”, “Private” definitions
- “Customer Content” definition
- “Data residency” vs “data processing region”
- “Audit log” vs “application logs”
- “No training on customer data” definition + any opt-in phrasing

Open questions
- Decide if we want glossary at top or bottom.


15) Versioning, change log, and how Sales should cite
Owner: Talia Benson
Include
- Versioning policy (monthly/quarterly)
- Who approves changes
- Where change log lives
- “Do not copy old PDF screenshots into RFPs” reminder

Sources
- Confluence: security-faq-change-log-2025-2026
- Slack: #sales/1768729031 (where final language lives)


High-risk phrasing checklist (add to end of draft for reviewers)
- ISO 27001: do not say “certified” unless verified.
- Residency: do not guarantee “EU-only” unless we can meet it by architecture + contract.
- Pen tests: do not claim a frequency unless Security/GRC confirmed.
- “No customer data stored”: likely false/overbroad; specify what is stored and for how long.
- “Fully single tenant”: avoid unless technically and contractually true.

Open questions tracker (to resolve before publish)
1) Data retention defaults + configurability (all data types, all modes) — owner: Olga Petrov / Marcus Lin
2) Audit log export: supported destinations + limitations — owner: Kevin Osei
3) RBAC/SCIM current behavior: groups, role mapping — owner: Markus Klein
4) Dedicated isolation language: what is actually dedicated — owner: Naomi Feldman / Markus Klein
5) ISO wording final — owner: Daniel Carter
6) HIPAA/BAA stance by mode — owner: Michael Grant (Legal) + Olga Petrov
7) Private telemetry list (what leaves customer env) — owner: Colin O’Donnell

Notes from field (themes to address explicitly)
- “Do you train on our prompts?” (must be unambiguous)
- “Can you meet EU residency?” (must be nuanced + mode-based)
- “Do you have audit logs and can we export to SIEM?” (give crisp yes/no + how)
- “Do you support SSO/SCIM?” (list what is supported today)
- “How fast can you share SOC 2 report?” (process + NDA)

Formatting notes (Confluence)
- Use collapsible sections per domain.
- Each answer should have:
  - Short answer (1–2 sentences)
  - Mode-specific notes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
  - Where to go next (link to one-pager / docs / evidence process)
  - Approved snippet id (if available)

TODOs (Talia)
- [ ] Convert this outline into Confluence page skeleton (headers + owner tags)
- [ ] Add link placeholders to each one-pager draft (SOC2 / ISO / residency / encryption)
- [ ] Confirm final reviewer list + sign-off order (Security -> GRC -> PM -> PMM -> Legal if needed)
- [ ] Create a single “claims we do/don’t say” callout at top (link to guidance page)
